title: ‘साल्गीको बलात्कृत आँसु’ कथामा वर्गीय द्वन्द्व {Class Struggles in Salgi's Raped Tears}
nepali: प्रस्तुत ‘साल्गीको बलात्कृत आँसु’कथामा वर्गीय द्वन्द्व शीर्षकको आलेख माक्र्सवादी वर्गीय चिन्तनका कोणबाट कथालाई विश्लेषण गर्ने उद्देश्यले तयार पारिएको हो । आलेख तयार पार्ने सन्दर्भमा मूलतः पुस्तकालय कार्यको उपयोग गरी संकलन गरिएका प्राथमिक र द्वितीयक स्रोतका सामग्रीहरूको अध्ययनबाट प्राप्त तथ्यलाई तर्क, प्रमाण÷साक्ष्य र उदाहरणका आधारमा पुष्टि गरिएको छ । कथामा प्रयुक्त ल्वाँगे घर्ती, सरदार्नी लगायतका पात्रहरूले शोषक र सामन्त वर्गको प्रतिनिधित्व गरेका छन् भने साल्गी, साल्गीकी आमा, आवा लगायतका पात्रहरूले शोषितपीडित वर्गको प्रतिनिधित्व गरेका छन् । खासगरी ल्वाँगे घर्तीजस्तो दलालले गाउँकी सोझी केटी साल्गीलाई आर्थिक प्रलोभनमा पारी जागिर लगाइदिने बहानामा कानपुरको वेश्यालयमा पु¥याई नारकीय जीवन बिताउन बाध्य बनाएको छ । साल्गीको देह व्यापारबाट वेश्यालयकी मालिक्नी सरदार्नी रातारात धनी बनेकी छ तर साल्गी जीर्ण शरीर र विदीर्ण हृदय लिएर गाउँ र घरपरिवारको सम्झनालाई केवल हृदयमा सजाएर बाँच्न विवश छ । वर्गीय चिन्तनका कोणबाट कथालाई दृष्टिगत गर्दा कथाका निम्नवर्गीय पात्रहरू गरिबी÷अभाव र अशिक्षाको शिकार, यौन शोषण र प्रताडना, लैङ्गिक उत्पीडनबाट आक््रmान्त छन् । यति हुँदाहुँदै पनि निम्नवर्गीय पात्रहरू सम्भ्रान्त वर्गको शोषणका विरुद्ध सशक्त रूपमा उत्रिएका छन् । सम्भ्रान्त वर्गका पात्रहरूको क्रुरतापूर्ण व्यवहारका विरुद्ध निम्नवर्गीय पात्रहरूले सङ्घर्ष र विद्रोहको आगो ओकलेका छन् । कार्ल माक्र्सले भनेझैँ सम्भ्रान्त वर्गको शोषण र उत्पीडनबाट मुक्ति पाउनका लागि निम्नवर्गीय पात्रहरूले गरेका प्रयत्नका कारण कथा वर्गीय द्वन्द्वका कोणबाट सफल देखिएको छ ।
american_english: The present article, titled 'Class Conflict in the Story "Salgi's Raped Tears"', has been prepared with the objective of analyzing the story from the perspective of Marxist class thought. In the context of preparing the article, facts obtained from the study of primary and secondary source materials collected chiefly through the use of library work have been verified on the basis of logic, evidence/testimony, and examples. The characters used in the story, Lwange Gharti, Sardarni and others, represent the exploiting and feudal class, while the characters Salgi, Salgi's mother, Aawa and others represent the exploited and oppressed class. In particular, a broker like Lwange Gharti, enticing Salgi, a simple village girl, with economic temptation and on the pretext of getting her a job, took her to a brothel in Kanpur and forced her into a hellish life. Through the trade of Salgi's body, Sardarni, the madam of the brothel, became rich overnight, but Salgi, with a worn-out body and a shattered heart, is forced to live decorating her heart only with the memory of her village and family. Viewing the story from the perspective of class thought, the lower-class characters of the story are victims of poverty/deprivation and illiteracy, and are afflicted by sexual exploitation and torment and by gender oppression. Even so, the lower-class characters rise up strongly against the exploitation of the elite class. Against the cruel behavior of the elite-class characters, the lower-class characters have spewed the fire of struggle and rebellion. As Karl Marx said, because of the efforts made by the lower-class characters to attain liberation from the exploitation and oppression of the elite class, the story appears successful from the perspective of class conflict.

informal_english: So this piece — 'Class Conflict in the Story "Salgi's Raped Tears"' — was written to dig into the story through a Marxist class lens. For research it mostly leaned on library work, going through primary and secondary stuff, then backing the findings up with logic, evidence and examples. In the story, characters like Lwange Gharti and Sardarni are the exploiters, the feudal class, while Salgi, her mom and Aawa are the exploited, oppressed class. The real gut-punch is Lwange Gharti, a lowlife broker who dangled money in front of Salgi, a simple village girl, swearing he'd get her a job — but instead he took her to a brothel in Kanpur and forced her into a living hell. Thanks to selling Salgi's body, Sardarni, the brothel madam, got rich overnight, while Salgi — worn-out body, shattered heart — is left holding nothing but memories of her village and family in her heart. Through a class-conflict lens, the lower-class characters are victims of poverty, deprivation and illiteracy, hit by sexual exploitation and abuse, and crushed by gender oppression. Still, even with all that, they rise up strong against the elite's exploitation. Against the elite's cruelty, the lower-class characters spit the fire of struggle and rebellion. Just like Karl Marx said, because the lower-class characters fight so hard to break free from elite exploitation and oppression, the story works — it lands as a success from a class-conflict perspective.
